learning_objective: 🎯 Become a master sentence builder by using conjunctions to glue words, phrases, and clauses together perfectly!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔗 What is a Conjunction? (The Grammar Glue)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Conjunctions are joining words. They act like super-glue in English, connecting words, phrases, or entire sentences together so you do not sound like a robot. Instead of saying 'I like apples. I like bananas', you say 'I like apples AND bananas'.

These connect two equal parts of a sentence. Just remember the secret word FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So. Example: 'I wanted to play outside, BUT it was raining.' Both sides of the 'but' are independent clauses!

These join an independent clause (the strong engine) to a dependent clause (the weak coach). Words like Because, Although, Since, When, and If. Example: 'I stayed inside BECAUSE it was raining.' 'Because it was raining' cannot stand alone!

These conjunctions always travel in pairs! They work together to link parts of a sentence. Examples: Either/Or, Neither/Nor, Not only/But also, Both/And. Example: 'You can have EITHER chocolate OR vanilla ice cream.'

These words connect two separate sentences to show how ideas flow. Words like However, Therefore, Meanwhile, and In addition. We usually put a period before them and a comma after them! Example: 'It was raining. HOWEVER, we still played football.'

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The FANBOYS Master
fun_activity.instructions: Write down the letters F-A-N-B-O-Y-S on a piece of paper. Try to write one compound sentence for every single letter! (Hint: For means 'because', Yet means 'but').

quick_recap: ⭐ Conjunctions join words, phrases, or clauses together.
⭐ Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS) join equal, independent clauses.
⭐ Subordinating conjunctions (because, if, when) join a weak clause to a strong main clause.
⭐ Correlative conjunctions work in pairs like 'either...or' and 'neither...nor'.
⭐ Connectors like 'however' and 'therefore' show the flow of ideas between two separate sentences.
